samples.summary: The new triage comment layout breaks `parsePanelComment`, the corpus reader that parses the on-demand review comment — every on-demand review will now yield ZERO blocking findings, turning real panel hits into false "misses" in the eval corpus.
samples.evidence:
`scripts/agent/harvest.mjs` reads the posted on-demand comment body back as data (it says so explicitly: "Its findings exist only as markdown in the comment it posts… So this reads the comment"). It hard-codes the `renderSummaryMd` layout:
- `harvest.mjs:403` `PANEL_SECTION_RE = /^###\s+(Critical|Major|Minor|Nit|Demoted)\b/` — the new region emits `#### 🚫 Blocking (N)` and no `### Critical` / `### Major` headings at all; `harvest.mjs:441` (`/^###/` → `severity = null`) then guarantees `severity` is never set, so no row is ever collected.
- `harvest.mjs:408` `PANEL_FINDING_RE = /^[-*]\s+`([^`]+)`\s*[—–-]\s*(.+)$/` requires a backtick immediately after `- `. The new blocking row is `- **[`a.ts:5`](https://…)** — boom <sup>Correctness</sup>` (review-comment.mjs `blockingHead`), which does not match; minor/nit rows are additionally inside `<details>` blocks.
- `harvest.mjs:404` `PANEL_LENS_RE = /review:\s+\*\*/` matches the per-lens `❌ Correctness review: **changes requested**` header that the triage region no longer emits.
Because the `<!-- agent-review:<sha> -->` marker still parses, `parsePanelComment` returns `{reviewedSha, findings: []}` rather than `null`, and `panelFindingsFromComments` reports the PR as reviewed-with-nothing-raised. Per that module's own documentation those parsed findings SUPPRESS CodeRabbit candidates, so the failure direction is the harmful one: every CodeRabbit blocker the panel actually caught is now recorded as a panel miss. `.trusted/scripts/agent/harvest.mjs:408` (the main copy the workflows actually execute) has the identical regexes, so running the trusted copy does not save it. Neither `harvest.mjs` nor its cross-renderer round-trip test (`scripts/agent/harvest.test.mjs:785-805`, and `.trusted/…/harvest.test.mjs:808` "rows enriched by the Phase 2 renderer still round-trip", which exercises `renderSummaryMd` only) is updated by this change. The fix belongs either in `harvest.mjs` (teach it the triage row/section shapes) or in `review-comment.mjs` (keep a parseable row form).

samples.summary: A non-gating (advisory) lens's critical/major findings are rendered under "🚫 Blocking" with no advisory marker, contradicting the green conclusion the panel wrote for that lens.
samples.evidence: `review-panel.mjs:2562-2566` writes `conclusion: "success"` and `advisory: true` for a non-blocking lens, and `severity.mjs::renderSummaryMd` renders its body as "ℹ️ advisory — not gating" precisely so a green check is not headed by a ❌. `collectLenses` (review-comment.mjs) carries `gating` through, but `renderReviewComment` uses it only for the overall header verdict — `bucketOf` keys on severity alone, so an advisory lens's findings land in the `🚫 Blocking (N)` section and the bold headline count as if they gated. Unreachable with today's `scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json` (every lens is `"gating": "blocking"`), which is why this is minor, but the advisory path exists in the orchestrator and any future advisory lens silently misreports.

samples.summary: DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS=60000 reserves "~5k" for the parts the workflow appends, but `ai-prompt.mjs` applies no length cap at all, so a findings-heavy review can still push the comment past GitHub's 65536 limit and fail the update.
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/ai-prompt.mjs` has no character budget anywhere (`renderAiPromptSection` emits one line per blocking finding, unbounded — a real review cited in the module header carried 38 blocking findings). The workflow builds `body = marker + region(≤~60k) + tally + promptSection + note` (agent-review-on-demand.yml:594) and its backstop at :600 slices to 64900 and then RE-APPENDS `tally + promptSection + note`, so once the prompt fold exceeds a few hundred chars the truncated body still exceeds 65536 and `issues.updateComment` 422s, stranding the "running" placeholder. The overflow path pre-dates this change (the old `bodies.join` was unbounded too), but the new fixed 60000 budget encodes an assumption about the prompt fold that its producer does not honour; a smaller region budget, or a cap in ai-prompt.mjs, would close it.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. harvest.mjs:403-408 hard-codes the renderSummaryMd layout (`^###\s+(Critical|Major|...)`, `^[-*]\s+`file`\s*—`, `review:\s+\*\*`), and grep shows no handling of the triage shapes anywhere in harvest.mjs (only prose at :411/:413); .trusted/scripts/agent/harvest.mjs:403-408 is identical. The new renderer emits `#### 🚫 Blocking (N)` (review-comment.mjs:243, :255), which fails PANEL_SECTION_RE but matches the `/^###/` reset at harvest.mjs:441, so severity is never set; and blockingHead (review-comment.mjs:87) emits `- **[`a.ts:5`](url)** — …`, which cannot match PANEL_FINDING_RE (backtick must follow `- `). The workflow reaches this path: agent-review-on-demand.yml:486-496 builds the region and :591-594 prefers it, prefixed by the `<!-- agent-review:<sha> -->` marker, so PANEL_COMMENT_RE (harvest.mjs:377) still matches and parsePanelComment returns {reviewedSha, findings: []} instead of null. harvest.mjs:1004/:1020-1022/:1063-1073 then treat that empty array as the affirmative "panel raised nothing blocking", so real panel hits become false misses in the eval corpus. No consumer or test was updated (harvest.test.mjs:785-811 covers only renderSummaryMd-shaped bodies). This is a changed rendered contract with an unupdated out-of-diff consumer — the blast-radius lane — and is blocking at major.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the repository. review-comment.mjs:27-29 documents a "~5k" reserve for the workflow-appended parts and sets DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS=60000, enforcing that budget only over its own region (:236). ai-prompt.mjs contains no length cap anywhere: renderAiPromptSection (:78-95) emits one unbounded line per fixable finding (:85), and the CLI (:126-144) writes it whole with no --max-chars option. The workflow composes body = marker + region + tally + promptSection + note (yml:594) and its backstop (yml:600) slices to 64900 and then RE-APPENDS tally + promptSection + note, so once the prompt fold exceeds a few hundred chars the "truncated" body still exceeds GitHub's 65536 limit; publish() (yml:518-520) is the terminal statement (:601) with no fallback, so the 422 strands the "running" placeholder. Neither invocation step supplies a cap (yml:472-478, yml:486-496) and a repo-wide grep for MAX_CHARS/65536/65000/64900 found no guard on this path. Arithmetic: ~45 marker + ~59.95k region + ~200 tally + ~130 note leaves only ~5.2k headroom, which a findings-heavy review (module header cites a real ~20k review; .agent-review artifacts show 8+ findings from one lens alone) can exceed. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane: a documented budget invariant in one module that a sibling producer does not honour, with the breaking site outside the changed file. Not refutable on any named ground.
